⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Even when artificial intelligence behaves exactly like a human, people are reluctant to consider it conscious, according to a new study from Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (LMU).
  • In a recent development, as artificial intelligence becomes more advanced, reports of AI systems misleading users, working together, or appearing to pursue independent goals are becoming increasingly common.
  • Newly introduced research from LMU suggests that people make a clear distinction between displaying intelligent behavior and possessing a conscious mind, even when humans and AI act in precisely the same way.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Even when artificial intelligence behaves exactly like a human, people are reluctant to consider it conscious, according to a new study from Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (LMU).

In a recent development, as artificial intelligence becomes more advanced, reports of AI systems misleading users, working together, or appearing to pursue independent goals are becoming increasingly common. These behaviors often lead people to describe AI as though it can think, feel, or make decisions for itself. But does behaving like a human actually convince people that a machine has consciousness?

Newly introduced research from LMU suggests that people make a clear distinction between displaying intelligent behavior and possessing a conscious mind, even when humans and AI act in precisely the same way.

How Scientists Tested Perceptions of AI Consciousness.

Published in the journal Cognition, the study was led by Dr. Louis Longin of LMU's Chair of Philosophy of Mind, working alongside Dr. Bahador Bahrami, Professor Ophelia Deroy, and other researchers.

"Whereas previous studies have typically asked general questions about whether AI actually has mental states, our study is the first to directly compare how people attribute the same mental states to AI and humans behaving in exactly the same way, under identical circumstances," says Longin.

"We may be using mental terms to refer to AI, but this may only be because we lack better words," claims Ophelia Deroy, philosopher and a senior author of the study. "After all, AI is trained to act and speak like a human, so these descriptions seem natural.".

Recent findings suggest that to investigate how people judge consciousness, the researchers conducted experiments involving nearly 1,100 participants. One group read brief descriptions of artificial agents that showed different levels of responsiveness to their environments. For example, some agents reacted to sounds or recognized the emotional states of others.

In a recent development, another group encountered the same situations, except the characters were described as humans rather than AI systems. Participants then evaluated how conscious or aware each character seemed to be of its surroundings.

A Surprising Gap Between Human and AI Consciousness.

It has been revealed that the experiments revealed that responsiveness influenced how participants judged both humans and artificial intelligence. Characters that reacted more actively to their surroundings were generally considered more conscious and more aware.

However, a striking difference emerged when participants evaluated consciousness specifically. Even the most responsive AI was rated as less conscious than the least responsive human. In other words, identical behavior did not lead people to assign the same level of consciousness to humans and machines.

Sources indicate that the results changed considerably when participants were asked about awareness instead. For this characteristic, judgments of humans and AI followed largely similar patterns, suggesting that people interpret awareness and consciousness in fundamentally different ways.

Recent findings suggest that "There is a growing worry in public discussion that people will see AI behaving in a human-like way and start treating these systems as if they had human-like mental states," notes Longin, lead author of the study. "We found something much more nuanced: People are quite willing to say that an AI notices things and is aware of its surroundings. But they clearly draw a line when it comes to the term 'consciousness'. People consistently attribute less consciousness to AI than humans -- even when their behavior is identical.".

Although people sometimes describe AI as conscious when discussing its actions, the findings indicate that they still distinguish between artificial systems and human minds.

Why One Word Changes How We Perceive AI.

The researchers believe the difference between consciousness and awareness offers an crucial insight into how people understand artificial intelligence.

According to recent reports, awareness is a relatively neutral term that can describe an agent's ability to detect and respond to information in its environment. Consciousness, however, carries deeper implications about subjective experience and what it means to have an inner mental life.

Recent findings suggest that because awareness focuses more directly on observable behavior, people appear comfortable applying it to both humans and AI. Consciousness carries a different meaning, leading people to judge the two much less similarly.

The findings also highlight why the language used to discuss artificial intelligence matters, particularly as AI systems become increasingly capable of producing convincing human behavior.

In a recent development, "Our study teaches us lessons for how we communicate about AI," says Bahador Bahrami, who is also a senior author of the study and an expert in social neuroscience. "Companies and journalists often reach for hyped descriptions of AI models, and credit them with intentions, plans, or even moral conscience and hesitation. What our study indicates is that everyday judgments are much more discriminating: People do not simply put AI and humans on the same mental scale. But the boundary also depends on which terms we use. For more neutral descriptors such as 'awareness', the distinction can largely disappear. That makes our choice of language important.".

#218395. People are taking an unapproved weight-loss drug. AI found something surprising

📅 22 Oct 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1433 w)
📖 Baca
AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Sciencedaily ↗ Open Full Page

People are taking an unapproved weight-loss drug. AI found something surprising

📅 22 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1433 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • An experimental weight-loss drug that has not yet received regulatory approval is already attracting people willing to obtain unapproved versions online.
  • In a recent development, the drug, retatrutide, belongs to a newly introduced generation of GLP-1 medications designed to help regulate appetite and body weight.
  • Sources indicate that researchers at the University of Pennsylvania analyzed nearly 150,000 Reddit posts and comments from approximately 40,000 users to investigate these accounts.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

An experimental weight-loss drug that has not yet received regulatory approval is already attracting people willing to obtain unapproved versions online. Now, scientists are using artificial intelligence to investigate their experiences, uncovering unexpected symptom reports that differ from those documented in clinical trials.

In a recent development, the drug, retatrutide, belongs to a newly introduced generation of GLP-1 medications designed to help regulate appetite and body weight. Although it remains under investigation and is not approved for use, people are purchasing unapproved formulations that are not intended for human consumption and discussing their experiences on internet forums.

Sources indicate that researchers at the University of Pennsylvania analyzed nearly 150,000 Reddit posts and comments from approximately 40,000 users to investigate these accounts. Their study, published in JAMA Network Open, provides the first systematic examination of potential side effects reported by people claiming to use unapproved retatrutide.

According to recent reports, one finding stood out. Among users whose reported symptoms could be classified, increased appetite was the most common complaint. That was particularly unexpected because retatrutide is designed to suppress hunger, and its Phase 2 clinical trials primarily identified digestive problems as the most frequent side effects.

AI Uncovers Unexpected Weight-Loss Drug Reports.

In a recent development, "Our goal is to identify hypotheses in online conversations that we could test. AI helps us find recurring patterns in people's self-reports, including experiences that may be missed by conventional drug-safety monitoring," says Sharath Chandra Guntuku, Research Associate Professor in Computer and Information Science (CIS), Director of Penn's Computational Social Listening Lab and senior author of the study.

Industry observers note that however, the researchers emphasize that the findings should not be interpreted as proof of previously unknown side effects. Reddit users represent a very different population from clinical trial participants, and their accounts cannot establish whether the drug caused the symptoms they described.

There is also considerable uncertainty about what these individuals are actually taking. Products sold outside regulated medical channels may differ from the genuine experimental medication in their ingredients, purity, and dosage.

"We can't say that retatrutide is causing these symptoms, or even that Reddit people are actually taking genuine retatrutide, since the drug is not legally available, and gray market formulations vary," indicates Lyle Ungar, Professor in CIS and a co-author of the study.

Rather than confirming new risks, the research offers scientists an opportunity to identify questions that warrant more rigorous investigation.

"This is the first glimpse into the experiences of a population that is otherwise outside conventional drug safety monitoring because they are taking unapproved versions of a drug that has yet to finish clinical trials," notes Neil Sehgal, the study's first author and a doctoral student in CIS.

How Researchers Analyzed 150,000 Reddit Posts.

Sources indicate that the project builds on previous research by the University of Pennsylvania team. In that earlier investigation, scientists used large language models (LLMs), the type of artificial intelligence that powers many modern chatbots, to examine more than 400,000 Reddit posts discussing semaglutide and tirzepatide.

That analysis revealed reports of possible side effects, including menstrual irregularities, that may not have been fully documented in clinical trials or official drug safety records.

"We wanted to apply the same methodology to gray-market retatrutide," notes Sehgal.

Retatrutide is particularly interesting because it works differently from existing GLP-1 medications. Semaglutide acts on one hormone receptor involved in blood sugar control and appetite regulation, while tirzepatide targets two. Retatrutide activates three receptors, potentially producing a different combination of effects throughout the body.

Sources indicate that to investigate what people were experiencing, the researchers used AI to examine nearly 150,000 Reddit posts and comments. They identified approximately 14,000 customers who claimed to have personally taken an unapproved version of retatrutide.

The AI systems then extracted descriptions of symptoms that customers associated with the medication and translated those descriptions into standardized medical terminology. This allowed researchers to compare reports even when different people used different words to describe similar experiences.

After excluding expected effects such as weight loss and reduced appetite, the team identified 7,823 owners who reported at least one symptom that could be medically classified.

"A researcher might be able to examine a few thousand Reddit posts by hand, but looking at nearly 150,000 would be an enormous undertaking," notes Sehgal. "AI makes it possible to analyze these conversations at scale, identifying patterns in what people are sharing that would otherwise be difficult to recognize.".

A Surprising Appetite Paradox Emerges.

The most striking difference involved hunger.

Sources indicate that in retatrutide's Phase 2 clinical trials (the drug is presently in Phase 3 trials, the final step before FDA approval), participants most commonly experienced gastrointestinal complaints, including nausea. These effects are familiar concerns with medications that influence appetite and digestion.

In a recent development, but among Reddit customers who reported taking unapproved retatrutide, the pattern looked different. Increased appetite emerged as the most frequently described classifiable symptom, despite the substantial weight-loss effects demonstrated in clinical testing.

The researchers also compared the new findings with their earlier analysis of semaglutide and tirzepatide.

Compared with those earlier Reddit reports, discussions involving unapproved retatrutide contained proportionally more mentions of appetite-related changes, sleep disturbances, increased heart rate, and muscle-related symptoms. Reports of nausea and other digestive complaints were proportionally less common.

These differences could reflect how retatrutide interacts with the body. However, they could also result from differences between the groups of people discussing the medications, their other drug use, or the contents of the unapproved products.

"Retatrutide works differently from existing GLP-1 drugs, so it's possible that its effects on the body are different, too," claims Jena Shaw Tronieri, Senior Research Investigator at Penn's Center for Weight and Eating Disorders and a co-author of the study.

According to recent reports, "But the people discussing it on Reddit also may be different," she notes. "Users willing to obtain an unapproved medication on the gray market likely differ from other clinical populations. Some may be taking multiple experimental peptides, and we can't verify exactly what they're taking. We need more research to understand what, if anything, these differences in self-reported symptoms mean.".

Can AI Detect Drug Safety Concerns Earlier?

Beyond the findings about retatrutide, the study demonstrates how AI could potentially improve the early detection of drug safety concerns.

Sources indicate that traditional monitoring systems depend heavily on clinical trials, reports submitted to regulators, and information collected by healthcare professionals. People obtaining experimental medications through unapproved channels may not be represented in those systems.

Social media offers another source of information, allowing researchers to identify recurring experiences that might otherwise escape attention. However, these reports must be independently investigated before they can be considered reliable evidence of a drug-related problem.

The Penn team has already seen an example of how this approach can help guide further research.

In their previous investigation of semaglutide and tirzepatide, researchers identified online reports of menstrual irregularities. Those findings subsequently encouraged another scientific team to examine similar symptoms using the FDA's database of reported adverse drug events.

According to recent reports, the follow-up study, published in Obstetrics & Gynecology, also detected disproportionate reports of certain menstrual changes. Although those findings did not establish causation, they provided additional reasons to investigate the potential connection.

The researchers hope their retatrutide findings will lead to similar independent studies, particularly as the drug advances through clinical development.

"That's what we hope will happen with this study," indicates Sehgal. "Other researchers can take what we find on Reddit and look for the same patterns in other datasets, using entirely different methods. Whether those signals hold up or not, the goal is to build a better understanding of what people are actually experiencing.".

Sources indicate that the research was conducted through the University of Pennsylvania's School of Engineering and Applied Science and Perelman School of Medicine. Benjamin Rader of Boston Children's Hospital also contributed as a co-author. Funding was provided in part by the University of Pennsylvania's Penn Medical Communication Research Institute. Tronieri disclosed receiving an investigator-initiated grant from Novo Nordisk on behalf of the University of Pennsylvania, along with consulting fees from Currax Pharmaceuticals, LLC. No conflicts of interest were reported by the other authors.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In our previous post, Exploring Quantization Backends in Diffusers, we dived into how various quantization techniques can shrink diffusion models like FLUX.1-dev, making them significantly more accessible for inference without drastically compromising performance.
  • In a recent development, performing inference is cool, but to make these models truly our own, we also need to be able to fine-tune them.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In our previous post, Exploring Quantization Backends in Diffusers, we dived into how various quantization techniques can shrink diffusion models like FLUX.1-dev, making them significantly more accessible for inference without drastically compromising performance. We saw how bitsandbytes, torchao, and others reduce memory footprints for generating images.

In a recent development, performing inference is cool, but to make these models truly our own, we also need to be able to fine-tune them. Therefore, in this post, we tackle efficient fine-tuning of these models with peak memory use under ~10 GB of VRAM on a single GPU. This post will guide you through fine-tuning FLUX.1-dev using QLoRA with the diffusers library. We'll showcase results from an NVIDIA RTX 4090. We'll also highlight how FP8 training with torchao can further optimize speed on compatible hardware.

We aim to fine-tune black-forest-labs/FLUX.1-dev to adopt the artistic style of Alphonse Mucha, using a small dataset.

The model consists of three main components:.

Sources indicate that in our QLoRA approach, we focus exclusively on fine-tuning the transformer component. The text encoders and VAE remain frozen throughout training.

According to recent reports, we used a diffusers training script (slightly modified from here designed for DreamBooth-style LoRA fine-tuning of FLUX models. Also, a shortened version to reproduce the results in this blogpost (and used in the Google Colab) is available here. Let's examine the crucial parts for QLoRA and memory efficiency:.

LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation) Deep Dive: LoRA makes model training more efficient by keeping track of the weight updates with low-rank matrices. Instead of updating the full weight matrix W W W, LoRA learns two smaller matrices A A A and B B B. The enhancement to the weights for the model is ΔW=BA \Delta W = B A ΔW=BA, where A∈Rr×k A \in \mathbb{R}^{r \times k} A∈Rr×k and B∈Rd×r B \in \mathbb{R}^{d \times r} B∈Rd×r. The number r r r (called rank) is much smaller than the original dimensions, which means less parameters to update. Lastly, α \alpha α is a scaling factor for the LoRA activations. This affects how much LoRA affects the updates, and is often set to the same value as the r r r or a multiple of it. It helps balance the influence of the pre-trained model and the LoRA adapter. For a general introduction to the concept, check out our previous blog post: Using LoRA for Efficient Stable Diffusion Fine-Tuning.

In a recent development, QLoRA: The Efficiency Powerhouse: QLoRA enhances LoRA by first loading the pre-trained base model in a quantized format (typically 4-bit via bitsandbytes), drastically cutting the base model's memory footprint. It then trains LoRA adapters (usually in FP16/BF16) on top of this quantized base. This dramatically lowers the VRAM needed to hold the base model.

Sources indicate that for instance, in the DreamBooth training script for HiDream 4-bit quantization with bitsandbytes reduces the peak memory usage of a LoRA fine-tune from ~60GB down to ~37GB with negligible-to-none quality degradation. The very same principle is what we apply here to fine-tune FLUX.1 on a consumer-grade hardware.

Sources indicate that 8-bit Optimizer (AdamW): Standard AdamW optimizer maintains first and second moment estimates for each parameter in 32-bit (FP32), which consumes a lot of memory. The 8-bit AdamW uses block-wise quantization to store optimizer states in 8-bit precision, while maintaining training stability. This technique can reduce optimizer memory usage by ~75% compared to standard FP32 AdamW. Enabling it in the script is straightforward:.

It has been revealed that gradient Checkpointing: During forward pass, intermediate activations are typically stored for backward pass gradient computation. Gradient checkpointing trades computation for memory by only storing certain checkpoint activations and recomputing others during backpropagation.

Industry observers note that cache Latents: This optimization technique pre-processes all training images through the VAE encoder before the beginning of the training. It stores the resulting latent representations in memory. During the training, instead of encoding images on-the-fly, the cached latents are directly used. This approach offers two main benefits:.

This section demonstrates the QLoRA configuration for the base model:.

Defining LoRA Configuration (LoraConfig): Adapters are added to the quantized transformer:.

Only these LoRA parameters become trainable.

Before we launch the QLoRA fine-tune we can save a huge chunk of VRAM and wall-clock time by caching outputs of text encoders once.

At training time the dataloader simply reads the cached embeddings instead of re-encoding the caption, so the CLIP/T5 encoder never has to sit in GPU memory.

By combining this with cached VAE latents (--cache_latents) you whittle the active model down to just the quantized transformer + LoRA adapters, keeping the whole fine-tune comfortably under 10 GB of GPU memory.

According to recent reports, for this demonstration, we leveraged an NVIDIA RTX 4090 (24GB VRAM) to explore its performance. The full training command using accelerate is shown below.

It has been revealed that configuration for RTX 4090: On our RTX 4090, we used a train_batch_size of 1, gradient_accumulation_steps of 4, mixed_precision="bf16", gradient_checkpointing=True, use_8bit_adam=True, a LoRA rank of 4, and resolution of 512x768. Latents were cached with cache_latents=True.

Training Time (RTX 4090): Fine-tuning for 700 steps on the Alphonse Mucha dataset took approximately 41 minutes on the RTX 4090 with train_batch_size of 1 and resolution of 512x768.

Output Quality: The ultimate measure is the generated art. Here are samples from our QLoRA fine-tuned model on the derekl35/alphonse-mucha-style dataset:.

This table compares the primary bf16 precision results. The goal of the fine-tuning was to teach the model the distinct style of Alphonse Mucha.

The fine-tuned model nicely captured Mucha's iconic art nouveau style, evident in the decorative motifs and distinct color palette. The QLoRA process maintained excellent fidelity while learning the new style.

The results are nearly identical, showing that QLoRA performs effectively with both fp16 and bf16 mixed precision.

For owners with NVIDIA GPUs possessing compute capability 8.9 or greater (such as the H100, RTX 4090), even greater speed efficiencies can be achieved by leveraging FP8 training via the torchao library.

We fine-tuned FLUX.1-dev LoRA on an H100 SXM GPU slightly modifieddiffusers-torchao training scripts. The following command was used:.

The training run had a peak memory usage of 36.57 GB and completed in approximately 20 minutes.

After training your LoRA adapters, you have two main approaches for inference.

One approach is to load your trained LoRA adapters on top of the base model.

For when you want maximum efficiency with a single style, you can merge the LoRA weights into the base model.

While we showcased results on an RTX 4090, the same code can be run on more accessible hardware like the T4 GPU available in Google Colab for free.

On a T4, you can expect the fine-tuning process to take significantly longer around 4 hours for the same number of steps. This is a trade-off for accessibility, but it makes custom fine-tuning possible without high-end hardware. Be mindful of usage limits if running on Colab, as a 4-hour training run might push them.

According to recent reports, QLoRA, coupled with the diffusers library, significantly democratizes the ability to customize state-of-the-art models like FLUX.1-dev. As demonstrated on an RTX 4090, efficient fine-tuning is well within reach, yielding high-quality stylistic adaptations. Furthermore, for owners with the latest NVIDIA hardware, torchao enables even faster training through FP8 precision.

MIT scientists build a tiny robot that swims using living muscle cells

📅 23 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1474 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that A swimming robot does not necessarily need a bulky motor or powerful mechanical parts to move through water.
  • Recent findings suggest that the engineers developed an extremely thin swimming robot that uses living muscle tissue to move its fins.
  • Sources indicate that by directing light onto either fin, the researchers can trigger muscle contractions that make the fin flap and push the robot through water.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that A swimming robot does not necessarily need a bulky motor or powerful mechanical parts to move through water. MIT researchers have demonstrated that a single, carefully engineered layer of living muscle cells can generate enough force to propel a tiny robot forward.

Recent findings suggest that the engineers developed an extremely thin swimming robot that uses living muscle tissue to move its fins. Described in a newly introduced study published in Advanced Functional Materials, the device has a flexible gel framework roughly the length and width of a stick of gum. The gel forms two fins, each coated with a layer of muscle cells far thinner than a human hair. These cells have been genetically modified to contract when exposed to light.

Sources indicate that by directing light onto either fin, the researchers can trigger muscle contractions that make the fin flap and push the robot through water. Adjusting which fin receives light and how frequently it is illuminated allows the team to control both its speed and direction.

In experiments, the remarkably thin robot successfully swam and turned through a simple underwater maze. At maximum speed, it covered approximately four times its body length per minute. Although that is much slower than an Olympic swimmer, who can travel up to 65 body lengths per minute, it is comparable to the swimming pace of a cow shark moving leisurely through the ocean.

In a recent development, "It takes a lot of force to move through water versus air," claims study author Ritu Raman, associate professor of mechanical engineering at MIT. "The robot's quite strong, given its size. ".

A Upcoming Generation of Robots Powered by Living Muscle.

The device represents the first demonstration of a very thin, two-dimensional robot that can move from place to place using living muscle tissue.

It has been revealed that most existing biohybrid robots rely on relatively large, three-dimensional structures made from laboratory-grown skeletal muscle. Producing these structures typically requires millions of cells. Raman explains that thinner designs could reduce manufacturing costs while potentially improving movement efficiency.

"At the moment, biohybrid robots from our group and others' are built from bulky, 3D chunks of lab-grown skeletal muscle that require millions of cells to fabricate," indicates Raman, who notes that thinner, less bulky designs such as the team's newly introduced bot could be cheaper to build and could move more efficiently. "We believe that biohybrid robots powered by living muscle could one day perform delicate jobs like exploring environments too fragile or unpredictable for conventional hardware, because living tissue is soft, responsive to its surroundings, and can heal itself.".

The MIT research team also included first author Maheera Bawa, along with Arielle Berman, Laura Schwendeman, Ferdows Afghah, and Seanbiron Johnson.

From Artificial Muscle to a Swimming Robot.

The new swimming robot builds on an earlier achievement by Raman's laboratory. Last year, the researchers created an artificial muscle disk inspired by the human iris, demonstrating how a thin layer of living cells could produce precisely controlled movements.

It has been revealed that for that project, the engineers patterned a gel disk with grooves extending outward from its center and forming concentric circles. They then placed living muscle cells on the surface, where the cells grew into a thin layer following the patterned channels.

When illuminated, the muscle tissue contracted in different directions, causing the disk to stretch and compress. Its movements resembled the way the iris of the human eye changes shape as the pupil expands or narrows.

The experiment established that researchers could grow extremely thin muscle layers in intricate arrangements and use light to control their movements along multiple directions.

"People hadn't seen this muscle architecture engineered from scratch before," Raman says. "And the cells were moving in multiple directions. But they only moved about 100 microns. From a robotics perspective, their movements were tiny.".

For the latest project, the researchers wanted to dramatically increase the amount of movement and force generated by the muscle cells. Their goal was to produce contractions powerful enough to propel a robot through water.

They determined that achieving this would require a better foundation for the living muscle tissue.

The earlier artificial iris had used fibrin, an exceptionally soft gel, as its underlying structure. However, the team found that fibrin could quickly shrink under the forces exerted by contracting muscle cells, limiting the effectiveness of the resulting movement.

To overcome this problem, the engineers investigated three characteristics of the gel foundation: its chemical composition, its stiffness, and the dimensions and geometry of the grooves used to organize muscle growth.

Recent findings suggest that "For engineering any type of tissue, it's known that these are knobs you can tune," Raman indicates. "And we wanted to optimize all these parameters to support live muscle cells.".

Engineering a Stronger Muscle-Powered Robot.

Finding the right supporting material required testing gels with different formulations, stiffness levels, and surface patterns.

According to recent reports, the researchers compared several groove shapes, including narrow channels with square profiles and longer channels with curved bottoms. They discovered that muscle cells aligned more effectively inside square-shaped grooves.

This alignment was key because muscle cells that grow in the same direction are more likely to merge into fibers. Those fibers can then form stronger muscle tissue that contracts in a coordinated way. The square grooves therefore provided a more effective structure for producing force.

The team also replaced fibrin with gelatin methacrylate (GelMA), a material commonly used to grow and engineer biological tissue.

Sources indicate that by adjusting the formulation of GelMA, the researchers produced supporting gels with varying degrees of stiffness. They then examined how muscle cells developed on each surface and measured their ability to generate force.

It has been revealed that stiffer gels produced the best results. On these firmer surfaces, muscle cells grew in better alignment and generated stronger contractions.

Sources indicate that the engineers next investigated how thick the gel should be. They determined that a film measuring approximately half a millimeter offered an effective balance. It was sturdy enough to support a single layer of muscle cells while remaining sufficiently lightweight to prevent the contracting cells from detaching from the surface.

Recent findings suggest that the team further improved muscle performance through a form of exercise. Repeated pulses of light stimulated the cells to contract, strengthening the muscle tissue before it was incorporated into the swimming robot.

How Light Makes the Living Robot Swim.

With the gel structure optimized and the muscle cells strengthened, the researchers assembled their swimming device.

In a recent development, the finished robot consisted of a thin gel framework divided into two fins. Both sides of the gel were patterned with square-bottomed grooves and covered with living muscle cells. As the cells developed, they fused into organized muscle fibers capable of contracting together.

Each fin could be activated independently using light, giving the researchers a simple way to control the robot's movements.

Recent findings suggest that "You can think of the robot as having two independent muscles," Raman notes. "If we shine a light on just one, only that muscle moves. If shining on both, they both flap.".

Recent findings suggest that to test the device, the researchers placed it inside a large petri dish filled with water. They then moved a light source by hand, illuminating the fins to guide the robot through a maze positioned inside the dish.

In a recent development, as the muscles contracted, the fins flapped and propelled the robot through the water. By changing the light stimulation, the engineers successfully controlled its movement and helped it navigate the obstacles.

Although the robot demonstrated the ability to swim and steer, its current shape remains relatively simple. The primary objective of the experiment was to establish that an exceptionally thin layer of engineered muscle tissue could generate enough force for swimming.

The researchers now strategy to refine the robot's body to improve its speed. Beyond demonstrating a newly introduced approach to biohybrid robotics, the technology could eventually be useful for monitoring aquatic environments or operating in locations where conventional rigid machines might cause damage.

"Our next goal is to optimize the body design to enable faster swimming," Raman says. "But even at slow swim speeds, one could imagine a muscle-powered swimmer being used for purposes like environmental monitoring in aquatic environments.".

The Office of Naval Research provided partial funding for this research.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that hugging Face transformers library is the standard for working with state-of-the-art models — from experimenting with cutting-edge research to fine-tuning on custom data. Its simplicity, flexibility, and expansive model zoo make it a powerful tool for rapid development.

It has been revealed that but once you're ready to move from notebooks to production, inference performance becomes mission-critical. That’s where SGLang comes in.

Industry observers note that designed for high-throughput, low-latency inference, SGLang now offers seamless integration with transformers as a backend. This means you can pair the flexibility of transformers with the raw performance of SGLang.

Let’s dive into what this integration enables and how you can use it.

SGLang now supports Hugging Face transformers as a backend, letting you run any transformers-compatible model with high-performance inference out of the box.

No native support needed — SGLang automatically falls back to Transformers when needed, or you can set impl="transformers" explicitly.

Let’s walk through a simple text generation example with meta-llama/Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct to compare both approaches.

transformers library is great for experimentation, small-scale tasks and training, but it's not optimized for high-volume or low-latency scenarios.

SGLang takes a different track, prioritizing efficiency with features like RadixAttention (a memory-efficient attention mechanism). Inference with SGLang is noticeably faster and more resource-efficient, especially under load. Here’s the same task in SGlang using an offline engine:.

Or you can spin a server and send requests:.

Note that SGLang also offers an OpenAI-compatible API, making it a drop-in replacement for external services.

Industry observers note that with the new transformers backend integration, SGLang can now automatically fall back to using transformers models it doesn’t natively support. This means in practice:.

This unlocks faster inference and optimized deployment (e.g enabling RadixAttention) without sacrificing the simplicity and versatility of transformers ecosystem.

Sources indicate that note that specifying the impl parameter is optional. If the model is not natively supported by SGLang, it switches to transformers implementation on its own.

Any model on the Hugging Face Hub that works with transformers using trust_remote_code=True and properly implements attention is compatible with SGLang. You can find the exact requirements in the official documentation. If your custom model meets these criteria, all you need to do is set trust_remote_code=True when loading it.

Kyutai Team’s Helium isn’t yet natively supported by SGLang. This is where transformers backend shines, enabling optimized inference without waiting for native support.

There are several key areas we are actively working on to enhance this integration:.

Performance Improvements: transformer models currently lag behind the native integration in terms of performance.Our primary objective is to optimize and narrow this gap.

VLM Integration: we are also working toward adding support for Vision-Language Models (VLM) to broaden the range of capabilities and use cases.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, gemma 3n was unveiled as a preview during Google I/O. The on-device community got really excited, because this is a model designed from the ground up to run locally on your hardware. On top of that, it’s natively multimodal, supporting image, text, audio, and video inputs 🤯.

Today, Gemma 3n is finally available on the most used open source libraries. This includes transformers & timm, MLX, llama.cpp (text inputs), transformers.js, ollama, Google AI Edge, and others.

This post promptly goes through practical snippets to demonstrate how to use the model with these libraries, and how easy it is to fine-tune it for other domains.

Here is the Gemma 3n Release Collection.

Two model sizes have been released today, with two variants (base and instruct) each. The model names follow a non-standard nomenclature: they are called gemma-3n-E2B and gemma-3n-E4B. The E preceding the parameter count stands for Effective. Their actual parameter counts are 5B and 8B, respectively, but thanks to improvements in memory efficiency, they manage to only need 2B and 4B in VRAM (GPU memory).

These models, therefore, behave like 2B and 4B in terms of hardware support, but they punch over 2B/4B in terms of quality. The E2B model can run in as little as 2GB of GPU RAM, while E4B can run with just 3GB of GPU RAM.

In addition to the language decoder, Gemma 3n uses an audio encoder and a vision encoder. We highlight their main features below, and describe how they have been added to transformers and timm, as they are the reference for other implementations.

Industry observers note that the easiest way to vibe check the model is with the dedicated Hugging Face Space for the model. You can try out different prompts, with different modalities, here.

Install the latest version of timm (for the vision encoder) and transformers to run inference, or if you want to fine tune it.

The easiest way to start using Gemma 3n is by using the pipeline abstraction in transformers:.

Initialize the model and the processor from the Hub, and write the model_generation function that takes care of processing the prompts and running the inference on the model.

Since the model supports all modalities as inputs, here's a brief code explanation of how you can use them via transformers.

Support for videos is done as a collection of frames of images.

Sources indicate that gemma 3n comes with day 0 support for MLX across all 3 modalities. Make sure to upgrade your mlx-vlm installation.

Industry observers note that in addition to MLX, Gemma 3n (text only) works out of the box with llama.cpp. Make sure to install llama.cpp/ Ollama from source.

Check out the Installation instruction for llama.cpp here: https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/docs/install.md.

Recent findings suggest that finally, we are also releasing ONNX weights for the gemma-3n-E2B-it model variant, enabling flexible deployment across diverse runtimes and platforms. For JavaScript developers, Gemma3n has been integrated into Transformers.js and is available as of version 3.6.0.

For more information on how to run the model with these libraries, check out the usage section in the model card.

Given the size of the model, it’s pretty convenient to fine-tune it for specific downstream tasks across modalities. To make it easier for you to fine-tune the model, we’ve created a simple notebook that allows you to experiment on a free Google Colab!

We also provide a dedicated notebook for fine-tuning on audio tasks, so you can easily adapt the model to your speech datasets and benchmarks!

According to recent reports, with this release, we also introduce the Hugging Face Gemma Recipes repository. One will find notebooks and scripts to run the models and fine tune them.

In a recent development, we would love for you to use the Gemma family of models and add more recipes to it! Feel free to open Issues and create Pull Requests to the repository.

We are always excited to host Google and their Gemma family of models. We hope the community will get together and make the most of these models. Multimodal, small sized, and highly capable, make a great model release!

According to recent reports, if you want to discuss the models in more detail, go ahead and start a discussion right below this blog post. We will be more than happy to help!

Costco is coming to the rescue of anyone scrambling to put together a last-minute Thanksgiving dinner, bringing back its affordable meal kit with enough food to feed up to eight people.

Earlier in November, Costco made headlines for selling a massive 30-pound Thanksgiving dinner for $200, complete with a turkey, numerous sides, and desserts.

However, that extravagant feast required customers to place their orders by November 13, leaving anyone who missed the deadline out of luck.

Thankfully, with just days to go until Thanksgiving, Costco has brought back a considerably cheaper alternative that doesn’t require a pre-order.

A post shared by Laura Jayne Lamb (@costcohotfinds).

As reported by Delish, Costco’s Kirkland Signature Turkey Dinner Kit has returned to the retailer’s deli department for 2026.

Each kit comes with a seasoned, boneless half turkey breast, herbed stuffing, Yukon Gold mashed potatoes, green beans, cranberry sauce, and gravy.

The kits are priced at $3.99 per pound and weigh around 10 pounds, meaning shoppers can expect to pay roughly $40 for the entire meal.

According to Costco’s official product listing, each kit serves seven to eight people, bringing the cost down to around $5 per person.

Industry observers note that while the turkey still needs to be cooked, much of the preparation has already been taken care of. The meat even comes sitting on top of the stuffing, allowing the juices to soak into it while roasting.

Unlike Costco’s more expensive Thanksgiving feast, however, the kit doesn’t include dinner rolls or dessert, so you might want to grab one of the retailer’s famous pumpkin pies while you’re there.

Sources indicate that costco isn’t the only retailer trying to make Thanksgiving more affordable. Walmart is offering a $35 feast that feeds 10 people, while Amazon has a $25 Thanksgiving meal with same-day delivery on qualifying orders.

Tech Report: Cambridge scientists create a $10 chip that could put a medical lab on your wrist

📅 23 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1303 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A new optical sensor costing just $10 could bring laboratory-level precision to wearable health monitors, potentially allowing people to track blood glucose without needles.
  • In a recent development, researchers at the University of Cambridge and GlitterinTech (a start-up founded by the same research group) have developed a new type of optical spectrometer that combines exceptional accuracy with a remarkably small size and low cost.
  • Optical spectrometers work by analyzing light to reveal information about the substances it interacts with.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A new optical sensor costing just $10 could bring laboratory-level precision to wearable health monitors, potentially allowing people to track blood glucose without needles. The technology could also transform food testing, industrial quality control, and environmental monitoring.

In a recent development, researchers at the University of Cambridge and GlitterinTech (a start-up founded by the same research group) have developed a new type of optical spectrometer that combines exceptional accuracy with a remarkably small size and low cost. Measuring just centimeters across, the device could be incorporated into portable electronics and wearable health technology. Its potential applications range from monitoring important health markers in real time to identifying materials and detecting changes in chemical composition.

Optical spectrometers work by analyzing light to reveal information about the substances it interacts with. They are essential tools in medicine, manufacturing, chemical testing, and environmental research. However, making these instruments smaller has traditionally meant compromising their performance. Compact spectrometers often have limited measurement ranges, reduced resolution, or lower accuracy, making them better suited to identifying substances than performing precise measurements.

Recent findings suggest that the researchers believe their newly introduced design could overcome these limitations. Known as a convolutional spectrometer, it uses a mathematical principle called the convolution theorem to analyze light in a fundamentally different way. According to the team, this approach delivers performance that surpasses existing types of spectrometers in several key areas, including designs based on light dispersion, Fourier transforms, and computational reconstruction.

A New Way to Analyze Light With Extraordinary Precision.

Traditional spectrometers generally separate incoming light into its component wavelengths or use complex calculations to reconstruct its spectrum. The fresh device takes another approach by performing a mathematical operation called convolution directly on the incoming light.

To accomplish this, the researchers arranged optical components with repeating spectral responses in a sequence. These components can include unbalanced Mach-Zehnder interferometers or micro-ring resonators. By adjusting them in proportion to one another, the system can shift its response to different wavelengths in a controlled, linear fashion. Fast Fourier transforms are then used to accurately recover the light spectrum.

"The key insight was to go back to the mathematics and ask whether there was a fundamentally cleaner way to retrieve spectra," said Dr. Chunhui Yao, a lead author of the study. "By using the convolution theorem directly in the optical domain, we avoid many of the limitations that have held miniaturized spectrometers back. This gives us high precision, strong noise tolerance, and very low computational overhead, all in a compact and low-cost system.".

According to recent reports, the researchers built the spectrometer using a silicon nitride photonic platform and integrated it with onboard electronics. It operates across a broad range of near-infrared wavelengths (1200-1700 nm) and can collect and process measurements in less than a second.

Another crucial advantage is its ability to expand its measurement capabilities without major hardware changes. Because the system uses repeating optical patterns, its spectral bandwidth can theoretically be extended almost without limit. Adding more optical components in sequence can also increase its resolution exponentially.

A $10 Sensor That Could Transform Food Testing and Healthcare.

It has been revealed that to evaluate the device outside purely theoretical measurements, the researchers tested it on a variety of materials and substances. The results demonstrated its potential for applications that normally depend on larger, more expensive laboratory instruments.

When used to identify plastics, pharmaceuticals, coffee, flour, and tea, the spectrometer achieved a 100% classification success rate in the reported tests. It also measured concentrations in water-based and organic solutions with accuracies of approximately 0.01%, exceeding the performance of commercial benchtop spectrometers in those experiments.

It has been revealed that the healthcare demonstrations were particularly promising. Under conditions designed to reflect real physiological environments, the device accurately measured several human biomarkers, including skin moisture, blood alcohol, blood lactate, and blood glucose.

The researchers also demonstrated noninvasive glucose tracking over an extended period in one participant. Although further testing would be needed before the technology could become a practical medical product, the finding suggests a possible route toward monitoring blood sugar without repeatedly piercing the skin.

It has been revealed that "These biomedical demonstrations are particularly exciting," stated Prof. Qixiang Cheng, who led the project. "What makes this work stand out is not just performance in the lab, but technical readiness. Dr. Chunhui Yao's contribution was crucial in translating a mathematical concept into a fully packaged, robust system that operates reliably across temperature extremes and real-world conditions. That combination is what opens the door to practical deployment.".

The sensor also demonstrated impressive resistance to temperature changes. It continued operating reliably between -20°C and 80°C, an unusually wide temperature range for a miniature spectrometer. This durability could be especially valuable for wearable devices, factory equipment, and sensors operating outdoors.

Why a Simpler Design Could Be a Major Breakthrough.

The new spectrometer's advantages extend beyond its accuracy, size, and price. Its internal design also reduces the amount of computing power needed to analyze incoming light.

Many existing miniature spectrometers depend on complicated calibration procedures and demanding algorithms to reconstruct spectral information. These methods can become unreliable when measurements contain noise, and they often require substantial processing resources.

Sources indicate that the Cambridge team's convolution-based approach avoids much of this complexity. Because the measurements follow a linear mathematical relationship, the system can recover spectra rapidly and consistently while using relatively little computational power.

"This is a beautiful example of how elegant engineering can unlock real impact," said Prof. Richard Penty, who contributed to the photonic system design and integration. "The architecture is simple, scalable, and manufacturable, yet it delivers precision that rivals or exceeds much larger instruments. Dr. Chunhui Yao played a central role in bringing together the photonic design, system integration, and experimental validation that made this possible.".

Its relatively simple construction could also make the technology easier to manufacture on a large scale, potentially bringing sophisticated optical measurements to devices where conventional spectrometers would be too bulky or expensive.

Bringing Laboratory-Grade Measurements to Everyday Devices.

The researchers envision a future in which accurate optical sensing becomes a routine feature of everyday technology rather than something largely confined to specialized laboratories.

In industrial settings, inexpensive spectrometers could be installed throughout manufacturing facilities to continuously check material composition and product quality. Similar sensors could monitor food freshness, identify substances, and analyze environmental conditions on a much larger scale than is currently practical.

Recent findings suggest that healthcare could see equally significant changes. Compact sensors might eventually enable wearables to measure hydration levels, detect signs of alcohol intoxication, track biomarkers related to physical fitness, or continuously monitor glucose levels for people managing diabetes.

Industry observers note that "Our vision is to make spectrometry as ubiquitous as temperature or motion sensing," added Prof. Qixiang Cheng. "This work reveals that high-quality spectral information doesn't have to be confined to the laboratory -- it can be embedded directly into the technologies people use every day.".

Sources indicate that as photonic technology becomes smaller and more advanced, the convolutional spectrometer provides a promising example of how mathematical insights and practical engineering can make sophisticated scientific instruments simpler, cheaper, and more accessible. By combining high precision with a device that costs around $10, the researchers have opened a potential path toward a new generation of smart sensors capable of measuring the hidden chemistry of our bodies and surroundings.

Scientists overcome a hidden obstacle to more powerful quantum computers

📅 26 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (970 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, silicon spin qubits could play a major role in the future of quantum computing because they can be produced using the same semiconductor manufacturing methods that make today's computer chips.
  • Researchers at the RIKEN Center for Emergent Matter Science and their collaborators have now made important progress toward solving this problem.
  • Leon Camenzind, a RIKEN research scientist and co-first author who supervised the experiments, explains the significance of the results: "This shows that high-fidelity control can be maintained even when several qubits are operated at the same time and represents an important step toward scaling up silicon-based quantum processors.".
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, silicon spin qubits could play a major role in the future of quantum computing because they can be produced using the same semiconductor manufacturing methods that make today's computer chips. However, researchers have faced a significant challenge. When multiple silicon qubits are controlled at the same time, their operations tend to become less accurate. Building practical, large quantum computers will require scientists to control many qubits simultaneously while keeping errors to a minimum.

Researchers at the RIKEN Center for Emergent Matter Science and their collaborators have now made important progress toward solving this problem. In a study published in Nature Physics, the team demonstrated highly accurate control of several silicon spin qubits operating simultaneously. Their experiments used an array of five qubits connected to a shared microwave control line. By identifying a major cause of errors during simultaneous operation, the scientists developed a technique to reduce those errors and maintain precision.

Leon Camenzind, a RIKEN research scientist and co-first author who supervised the experiments, explains the significance of the results: "This shows that high-fidelity control can be maintained even when several qubits are operated at the same time and represents an important step toward scaling up silicon-based quantum processors.".

Scientists Identify a Hidden Source of Quantum Computing Errors.

Unlike conventional computers, which store information as bits representing either 0 or 1, quantum computers use quantum bits, or qubits, that can exist in combinations of both states. Silicon spin qubits store this information using the spin of individual electrons confined within silicon. Performing reliable quantum calculations requires extremely precise control over these electron spins.

Microwave signals provide that control, but operating multiple qubits simultaneously can create unwanted effects that interfere with their accuracy. The researchers traced much of this problem to a phenomenon called the AC Stark shift.

Recent findings suggest that this effect occurs when microwave control signals alter a qubit's effective energy levels, producing changes in the phase of its quantum state. Those phase shifts can disrupt the intended operation of individual qubits, particularly when several are being controlled at once.

To counteract the problem, the team created a calibration method that compensates for these unwanted shifts. Rather than separately calibrating every possible combination of qubits, the technique relies on calibrations performed between pairs of qubits. This makes the approach more practical for systems containing larger numbers of quantum bits.

"Rather than requiring an entirely separate calibration procedure for every possible combination of qubits, our method uses calibrations between pairs of qubits to compensate for the unwanted phase shifts," explains Yi-Hsien Wu, the first author who carried out the experiments as part of his PhD research.

Quantum Qubits Achieve Accuracy Above 99.99%.

It has been revealed that the researchers combined their calibration technique with an improved device design and carefully adjusted microwave control pulses. Their results showed that exceptionally high accuracy could be maintained even when multiple qubits were operating simultaneously.

When the five qubits were tested individually, each achieved single-qubit gate fidelity well above 99.99%, with the highest approaching 99.999%. Fidelity describes how closely a quantum operation matches its intended result.

Sources indicate that the team then tested how well the system performed when several qubits were active together. With as many as three qubits operating simultaneously, fidelity remained above 99.99%. Even when all five qubits were controlled at once, accuracy stayed at approximately 99.9%, approaching the levels needed for practical fault-tolerant quantum computing.

Although the calibration method greatly reduced errors, it did not eliminate them entirely. The researchers found that the remaining loss of accuracy was linked to drive-induced decoherence, an effect caused by the greater microwave power required to operate multiple qubits simultaneously.

Unlike the unwanted phase shifts corrected by the new technique, decoherence involves the loss of the delicate quantum coherence needed for reliable operations.

According to Camenzind, "This is a limitation, but further improvements to device design could help mitigate this source of error.".

A New Path Toward Larger Quantum Processors.

Industry observers note that the findings show that controlling several silicon spin qubits at the same time does not necessarily require a major sacrifice in accuracy. By correcting a key source of errors, the researchers have demonstrated a promising approach for operating more qubits through shared microwave control lines.

This is especially important for the development of large quantum processors. Giving every qubit its own independent control system would make increasingly complex devices difficult to manage. Shared control lines could offer a more practical way to expand these systems while maintaining the precision needed for quantum calculations.

"By addressing a key source of control errors through pairwise calibration," says Camenzind. "Our study supports the use of shared control lines as a practical approach to scaling up quantum processors. Combined with silicon's compatibility with established semiconductor manufacturing, we believe that this advance could help pave the way toward larger quantum processors capable of performing increasingly complex computations.".

In a recent development, the broader objective is to develop quantum computers that can reliably perform calculations despite the errors and disturbances that affect quantum systems. Such machines, known as fault-tolerant quantum computers, will require precise, dependable control over large numbers of qubits.

"Our long-term goal is to build a fault-tolerant quantum computer based on silicon spin qubits, and reliable parallel control is an essential step toward that goal," adds Seigo Tarucha, project manager of a silicon quantum computing project under JST's Moonshot Goal 6.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that grand Theft Auto 6 is the greatest open-world simulation ever created. It is a breathtaking recreation of modern America, with extraordinary attention to detail and unrivalled freedom.

Industry observers note that vice City and the sprawling state of Leonida feel alive in ways no game has achieved before. Every street, random character, and minor interaction contributes to a world that feels like it exists beyond the player. It’s a technical achievement that raises the bar for open-world games forever.

For all its spectacle, ambition, and criminal excess, GTA 6 is also a deeply human story about two people trying to survive together in a world determined to tear them apart. And it’s the combination of unprecedented scale and genuine emotional depth that makes Rockstar’s latest masterpiece so extraordinary.

It has been revealed that grand Theft Auto 6 follows the story of Jason and Lucia, both fighting to make a name for themselves in Leonida after falling on hard times. We meet the two characters years before the events of the game, as they come across each other in Vice City, both stealing the same car.

According to recent reports, beyond that, Lucia is searching for answers about her family, mainly her child, after she lost custody following a stint in prison. As well as trying to pay the bills while working for Brian Heder, Jason is trying to find himself after serving in the army.

To both get what they’re looking for, they must build their way up from petty thieves to big-time bank robbers, all while dealing with what Leonida has to throw at them – it can get pretty wild, too.

Sources indicate that red Dead Redemption 2 was, for me, the greatest game ever made. Arthur Morgan’s story still remains my favorite in gaming, but what really made RDR2 special was the immersion. The Wild West felt totally real, making even the most ordinary activities enjoyable.

GTA 6 takes everything that made RDR2 so impressive and brings it to a modern-day recreation of Florida. It feels as though Rockstar took the best elements of Red Dead Redemption 2 and GTA 5 and amplified everything. The result is easily the most detailed open world ever created and quite possibly the best game of all time.

Sources indicate that leonida is absolutely packed with things to do. Whether you’re exploring the wilderness, discovering fresh locations, encountering wildlife, or investigating mysteries, there’s always something to keep you occupied.

It feels like there’s a fresh random encounter waiting around every corner, and in true Rockstar fashion, the developer seems to have thought of just about everything.

In a recent development, better yet, you’re rewarded for going off the beaten path. There’s so much to discover that simply taking a detour can be just as entertaining as progressing through the main story. This is a world that begs you to explore every inch of it, and it’s remarkably easy to lose track of what you originally set out to do.

It has been revealed that the attention to detail is on another level, too. Even everyday objects like books get more care than you’d expect, weapons can be customized to your heart’s content, and there are countless interactions that reward players for their creativity.

For instance, there’s one encounter early on where an NPC is filling his truck with gas. Players can flick a lit cigarette in his direction, triggering a massive gas station explosion.

Visually, GTA 6 is spectacular and as incredible as Vice City looks, the surrounding areas are equally impressive. From the lighting and weather effects to the character models and animations, the hardware has been pushed to its limits.

Industry observers note that there were so many times when I found myself driving down a highway or country road, simply marveling at the world. Towns feel genuinely lived in, complete with residential neighborhoods, commercial districts, strip malls, and a staggering number of interiors to explore. Even the traffic strikes a great balance between feeling authentic but never becoming so congested that it takes the fun out of driving.

The sheer amount happening on screen at any given moment is astonishing, especially considering the game’s graphical fidelity. There is a trade-off, however, with GTA 6 targeting 30 FPS on consoles. It’s disappointing not to have a smoother option, but given what has been accomplished with this world, it’s a compromise I’m willing to accept.

According to recent reports, the sound design is superb, too. The bustling streets of Vice City are alive with traffic, conversations, and background noise, while the quieter areas of Leonida have their own distinct atmosphere. The radio stations are another highlight, with a fantastic selection of music that makes even a leisurely drive across the map an enjoyable experience in its own right.

Thankfully, GTA 6 is every bit as fun to play as it is to explore.

According to recent reports, the missions are some of the best in a GTA game, with plenty of variety and outrageous moments that make the campaign a blast. There’s a great balance between the ridiculous situations we’ve come to expect from the series and the more serious story Rockstar wants to tell, without one ever undermining the other.

Much like RDR2, GTA 6 uses its early missions to introduce latest mechanics while gradually building toward something greater. There are some minor pacing issues in the opening hours, particularly with some of the more mundane tasks, such as fixing up the house for Lucia. It  takes its time establishing the world and its characters while allowing players to get a feel for how the game plays.

According to recent reports, but like any great symphony, there’s a gradual build before the crescendo. Once the training wheels start coming off midway through Chapter 2, and especially in Chapter 3, GTA 6 begins to unleash its full potential.

The revamped Wanted system, introduced relatively early on, adds an entirely upcoming dimension to police encounters. Cops now take your appearance, the vehicle you’re driving, and whether you’re carrying weapons into account, forcing you to be much more conscious of your actions when trying to evade the law.

It has been revealed that playing as Jason and Lucia together is an absolute blast, thanks to some of the best teammate AI I’ve ever experienced in a game. If you’re using a suppressed weapon, your partner will do the same. You can even work together to line up synchronized headshots.

According to recent reports, this isn’t some scripted interaction that requires a button press or an on-screen prompt like you’d find in an FPS campaign – the AI simply does it. Whether you’re controlling Jason or Lucia, it genuinely feels like you have a competent partner in crime and if you get caught or killed, it’s usually your own fault.

In a recent development, perhaps my favorite aspect of the gameplay, though, is the focus on robberies. They’ve come a long way since GTA 4’s legendary Three Leaf Clover mission. We saw Rockstar expand on the concept with GTA 5 and again with RDR2, but GTA 6 takes it to another level entirely. Even an ordinary bank robbery can be as exciting as a meticulously scripted action sequence from a Call of Duty campaign or the Uncharted series.

Sources indicate that early on in Chapter 3, I robbed a jewelry store with both characters, broke into a safe, and made off with the loot, only to find myself in a heated police chase. I let my partner take the wheel while I tried to hold off the cops hot on our trail.

It has been revealed that after putting some distance between ourselves and the police, but still not quite out of danger, I decided our best bet was to split up. I abandoned the main road, ran into the woods, and eventually stumbled across a farmhouse, where I stole another car and made my escape while my partner fenced the stolen goods.

What made the whole experience so memorable was that none of it felt like a carefully orchestrated mission. It was a situation I had got myself into and had to find my own way out of.

As you progress, you’ll acquire tools and skills that allow you to take a much stealthier approach, potentially pulling off robberies without the cops ever laying eyes on you.

It has been revealed that this is fun in its own right, as completing a brilliant heist without getting caught genuinely makes you feel like a badass. However, the occasions when things don’t go according to plan make for some of the most riveting gameplay GTA 6 has to offer.

In a recent development, there’s a very real sense of jeopardy, too. With death resulting in the loss of all the cash you’re carrying, there’s a sudden rush of adrenaline when a robbery goes sideways and you’ve got a small fortune on the line.

And that’s before even getting into the campaign’s major action set pieces, which are among the finest Rockstar has ever crafted. The finale of Chapter 1 is a particular standout and comfortably ranks among the greatest missions I’ve ever played in a video game.

Sources indicate that story-wise, GTA 6 had enormous shoes to fill following on from Red Dead Redemption 2. Unfortunately, neither Jason or Lucia are written with as much depth and growth as Arthur Morgan or other key members of the Van der Linde gang. A lot of that comes down to Jason’s dialogue and his personality being quite dry compared to other GTA characters.

Dylan Rourke, who voices Jason, has his moments, and without getting into spoiler territory, there are some emotional moments where he nails it. However, he seems to have had a lot less to work with than Manni L. Perez, who helps make Lucia the more compelling of the two.

It has been revealed that that said, GTA 6’s MacGuffins do a fantastic job at keeping interest incredibly high and driving the main plot in between side missions. And we are comparing it to what I think is the greatest video game story of all time.

Leonida is the most impressive open world I’ve ever explored, the missions are fantastic, and Jason and Lucia deliver a fine story that lives up to the brilliant world around them.

After more than a decade of waiting, Rockstar has delivered something truly special. GTA 6 isn’t just a worthy successor to GTA 5 and RDR2. It sets a upcoming standard, not just for what open-world games can achieve, but for gaming itself.

Grand Theft Auto 6 is the greatest open-world simulation ever created. It is a breathtaking recreation of modern America, with extraordinary attention to detail and unrivalled freedom.
